115E Inboard
Engineered for Builders
Built for Operators

The most integrated system, now below deck. A drive-to-throttle solution designed for boat builders, optimized for serious operators. 115hp inboard motorskid, 400V battery, controls and fast charging, specified and supported as one unit.

Below Deck

Drop it in. Bolt it up. Cast off.

The 115E Inboard is a complete electric motorskid: motor, inverter, cooling and 12V supply on one 120kg assembly, built to take the place of a fuel engine ahead of a Mercury Alpha or Bravo 3 sterndrive.

Fits the sterndrive you already trust.

Engineered around Mercury Alpha and Bravo 3 drives, so the hull, transom and lower unit stay as they are. One skid replaces the engine; the drive stays.

120 horses, continuously.

92kW at the motor shaft all day, with 161hp (120kW) on tap for the hole shot, and 270Nm of peak torque from zero RPM, up to 5,500 RPM.

Sealed, liquid-cooled, connected.

IP67 throughout, closed-loop liquid cooling, electric throttle, a 7" HD display and LTE, Bluetooth and Wi-Fi, with a built-in 12V supply (2.5kW continuous, 3kW peak) for the boat's house loads.

Fuel and energy costs only — excludes oil, winterization, and engine maintenance, where electric typically saves further. Defaults assume ~5 gal/hr average burn for a 115hp-class gas sterndrive across a mixed cruise profile, and ~30kW average draw for the 115E Inboard at comparable speeds. Zip code loads statewide averages: AAA road gasoline (July 2026) and EIA residential electricity (March 2026). Fuel-dock pricing adds $1.60/gal over road retail — posted dock prices sampled in July 2026 ran $1.20/gal above road averages on Long Island Sound and $1.94/gal above on Florida's Gulf Coast. Marina shore power and commercial or time-of-use rates are often below the residential average shown. Edit any field to match your actual costs. Estimates, not quotes.
